claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me begin with my first question:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is 17, there are some specific rules about Child Benefit eligibility at that age. Let me ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - doing A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that. That's an important detail since Alex is in approved education.

Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. That's very helpful.

Now I need to ask about your residency status in the UK:

**Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme? Or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

I have one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you or your partner (if you have one) earning over £60,000 per year individually?**

(This is relevant because there's a tax charge that applies to Child Benefit if individual income exceeds this threshold, though it doesn't affect eligibility itself.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, no - neither of us earns anywhere near that amount.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility.

Let me summarize your situation and provide my outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!** ✓

Here's why you qualify:

- **Age and Education:** Alex is 17 and still in approved education (A-levels at sixth form college). The rules allow you to claim Child Benefit for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training.
- **Responsibility:** You live with Alex, which means you are responsible for them.
- **Residency:** You are a UK citizen living in the UK.
- **No barriers:** There are no income restrictions or other factors preventing your claim.

If you haven't already claimed, you should be able to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you need to make a claim or have any other questions, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further support.
